object.practice: Keep planning, reasoning, tool selection, and result interpretation distinct enough that failures can be attributed to the stage that produced them.
Prefer observable tool results and repository state over assumptions made during model reasoning.
Preserve enough turn provenance to reconstruct why an action occurred without making internal reasoning itself part of the execution contract.
Treat session identity and turn identity as stable durable identifiers rather than deriving them from presentation-layer state.
Make session continuation deterministic with respect to persisted conversation state, configuration, and execution context.
Separate recoverable persisted state from ephemeral process-local state so interrupted sessions can resume cleanly.
Keep thread ordering explicit and preserve the causal order of turns and events.
Do not let presentation concerns mutate canonical thread state.
Persist history in a form that remains readable across process restarts and compatible schema evolution.
Record enough provenance to distinguish user input, model output, tool invocation, tool result, and system-generated events.
Construct context from explicit session state and relevant artifacts rather than ambient process state.
Keep context assembly reproducible so the source of an unexpected model behavior can be inspected.
Avoid duplicating large unchanged context when a stable reference or canonical representation is available.
Give every tool a clear input contract, output contract, and failure representation.
Keep tool discovery separate from tool execution so capability enumeration does not cause side effects.
Return structured execution results whenever downstream agent logic must distinguish success, partial success, rejection, and failure.
Capture command, working directory, exit status, stdout, and stderr as distinct execution data.
Do not infer command success from output text when the process provides an authoritative exit status.
Preserve the actual environment and working-directory context needed to reproduce a command failure.
Apply patches against explicit file state and report conflicts instead of silently approximating the requested change.
Keep modifications localized to the requested files and hunks unless the operation explicitly requires broader changes.
Return the resulting changed-file set so later verification operates on what actually changed.
Return source identity and location with search results so retrieved evidence remains traceable.
Distinguish an empty result from a failed, truncated, or inaccessible search.
Centralize execution decisions so equivalent operations receive equivalent treatment regardless of which interface initiated them.
Keep execution control separate from tool business logic so permissions and isolation behavior remain inspectable and reusable.
Represent denial, required approval, sandbox limitation, and execution failure as distinct outcomes.
Make sandbox boundaries explicit to the executor rather than relying on undocumented environmental behavior.
Report sandbox-caused failures distinctly from failures produced by the invoked operation itself.
Bind approval to the concrete operation being authorized so materially changed operations require a new decision.
Preserve approval outcome and operation identity as execution provenance.
Evaluate policy from the actual requested operation and execution context rather than from presentation-layer labels.
Keep policy decisions explainable in terms of the rule and operation that produced the decision.
Keep command semantics stable across interactive and non-interactive surfaces even when their presentation differs.
Return meaningful process exit codes for automation-facing commands.
Keep human formatting separate from machine-readable output modes.
Preserve long-running session state across incremental user interactions without requiring callers to reconstruct it manually.
Surface tool activity, failures, and state transitions clearly enough for the operator to understand what the agent is doing.
Avoid prompts requiring human interaction unless the invocation explicitly requests an interactive behavior.
Provide structured output and deterministic exit behavior suitable for scripts and CI systems.
Keep protocol handling separate from agent-domain state transitions so transport changes do not redefine runtime behavior.
Treat thread and turn lifecycle transitions as explicit operations with identifiable state.
Make streamed events ordered and attributable to their originating thread, turn, and operation.
Version protocol structures when compatibility cannot be preserved through additive change.
Prefer additive evolution over changing the meaning of an existing field or event.
Define terminal, error, cancellation, and partial-progress states explicitly rather than encoding them as ordinary messages.
Expose host-language abstractions without hiding important underlying lifecycle, error, and cancellation semantics.
Keep subprocess or transport details behind the client API while preserving actionable error information.
Support explicit start, resume, cancellation, and result-consumption operations rather than inferring lifecycle from object existence.
Keep extension discovery, enablement, loading, and invocation as distinct lifecycle operations.
An extension that fails to load should identify itself and its failure without making unrelated extensions indistinguishable from the failure.
Expose extension-provided capabilities through the same callable abstraction used for native capabilities where their semantics are equivalent.
Treat MCP server capability discovery as runtime data rather than assuming a fixed server tool catalog.
Preserve server identity with discovered capabilities so calls and failures remain attributable to the correct provider.
Keep plugin enablement explicit and separate from plugin discovery.
Do not require importing or initializing unrelated plugins to determine that they exist.
A plugin failure should remain attributable to that plugin rather than appearing as a generic host failure.
Separate connector authentication state from the capability contract exposed to the agent.
Return provider-originated errors with enough context to distinguish authentication, transport, authorization, and application failures.
Keep skill instructions self-contained enough that the runtime can determine when and how they apply.
Treat skills as reusable guidance rather than silently changing unrelated runtime semantics.
Define hook invocation points and ordering explicitly.
Prevent hook execution from silently changing the canonical meaning of the event it observes.
Make hook failure visible to the lifecycle that invoked it when that failure affects the operation.

join.practice: Pass session state through an explicit session abstraction rather than allowing the agent to reconstruct state independently on every turn.
Persist the state required for continuation before reporting a turn as durably complete.
Require tool actions to pass through the registered tool runtime so execution, result handling, and provenance remain consistent.
Return actual tool outcomes to the agent rather than synthesizing expected outcomes from the requested action.
Apply execution controls before the effect occurs, while preserving the original requested operation for later inspection.
Do not encode execution-control decisions into agent reasoning when they belong to the execution-control layer.
Translate command input into the same internal task representation used by other supported client surfaces.
Keep command parsing and display formatting outside the agent's core behavior.
Expose agent lifecycle operations through stable server contracts instead of leaking internal runtime objects across the boundary.
Map runtime state changes to server events without inventing an independent second lifecycle model.
Keep the protocol representation faithful to canonical session state while allowing protocol-specific serialization details to remain outside the runtime model.
Ensure every externally visible lifecycle transition has an unambiguous protocol representation.
Associate every dispatched tool action and result with its originating session and turn.
Complete or terminate outstanding tool operations explicitly when a turn is cancelled or interrupted.
Route effectful execution through the control layer without duplicating policy decisions inside individual tool handlers.
Preserve the tool's requested operation unchanged until the control layer has evaluated it.
Normalize extension-provided capabilities into the tool runtime's normal discovery and invocation contracts.
Preserve extension provenance so a capability can be traced back to the extension that supplied it.
Let the command interface consume the server lifecycle rather than recreating thread and turn orchestration independently.
Translate server events into terminal presentation without changing their semantic meaning.
Keep session creation, lookup, resume, and termination centralized behind explicit runtime operations.
Do not let client connection lifetime implicitly define session lifetime unless that relationship is part of the declared contract.
Validate incoming protocol messages before they mutate application-server state.
Serialize canonical lifecycle state rather than maintaining a second independently mutable protocol-state representation.
Treat the command process as a defined transport boundary with explicit startup, streaming, cancellation, termination, and error behavior.
Avoid parsing human-oriented terminal prose when a structured command output is available.
Register only capabilities actually supplied by enabled and successfully loaded extensions.
Remove or deactivate an extension's contributed capabilities when that extension becomes unavailable rather than leaving stale callable entries.
